findings.description: Phase 2.5 puts confirmation detection on the existing contradiction read rather than a pass of its own, scopes eligibility to `status: accepted`, leaves the five-read budget sentence verbatim and explicitly unraised, and states the stamp bypasses phase 5.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md:59-71,83. The numbered list is unchanged at five steps (verified: `sed -n '53,84p' | grep -cE '^[0-9]+\. '` returns 5 against both `git show 924f81f:inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md` and the working tree), so no numbered step with its own reads was added. :67 hangs detection off step 5's body read — "That read answers two questions rather than one: does this input contradict what the record claims, or does it restate it? ... Deciding an input doesn't contradict a record means you have already read everything the second question needs, so the confirmation costs nothing past the read that was happening anyway." :69 keeps the pinned sentence intact and hardens it — "**Five body reads per input, and the budget binds.** ... Confirmations come out of that same budget rather than drawing one of their own. There is no second pass over the records, and no sixth read on the grounds that an input might also be confirming something." :71 — "Only `status: accepted` records produce flags, and only they can be confirmed." :83 — "there is nothing for the user to sign off on and the stamp never passes through phase 5."

findings.description: Phase 6 requires both lists by name as imperative hand-check bullets, and the skipped list is scoped to the stamper's own `skipped:` lines rather than to everything phase 2.5 opened.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md:204,211-212. Both bullets sit under the imperative "Then check by hand what the lint can't:" at :204, so neither is optional. :211 — "Every record whose `last_confirmed` the run stamped is named, with the date it now carries. Read them off the stamper's `stamped:` lines. This report is the only durable trace of a write the user was never asked to approve." :212 names all four stage-2 skip branches and scopes the list explicitly — "Every record the stamper declined to write is named, with its reason: a v1 file, a `status` other than `accepted`, a date already at or past the note's, or an insertion that would overrun the 20-line frontmatter budget. Read them off its `skipped:` lines, which is also the scope of this list: what the stamper turned down, not everything phase 2.5 opened." That maps one-to-one onto the constitution's v1 / non-`accepted` / not-later / over-budget branches.

findings.description: The collision C-10 warns about does not occur: `grep -niE 'sanctioned|exception'` finds exactly two exception claims in the Operating Rules list, each naming the rule it excepts inside its own sentence, and the phrase "sanctioned exception" appears exactly once in the whole file.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md:476-486, read whole and in order. The new bullet is fifth of nine, at :482 — "**`last_confirmed` is written without sign-off.** The gate on `_memory/` — no file written until the user approves that item — has one exception, and this is it." The excepted rule is restated inline as an appositive, so the claim never travels unattached. The VTT bullet is ninth, at :486 — "This is the one sanctioned exception to preserving raw content exactly as captured" — naming its own rule, which is bullet two at :479 ("**Preserve raw content as the source of truth.**"). Three unrelated bullets (:483, :484, :485) separate the two, and the new bullet deliberately avoids the words "sanctioned exception" entirely: `/usr/bin/grep -niE 'sanctioned|exception' inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md` returns "sanctioned" on :486 alone. A reader finishing the list holds two exceptions, each bound to a different named rule, not two unattached claims to being the only one. Boundedness and reasoning are both present at :482: still-gated surface named ("Everything else stays gated: creating a record, amending one, superseding one, changing a word of what one claims"), metadata-not-content ("a date recording when the claim was last seen to hold, never the claim itself"), and the rubber-stamping argument ("A prompt whose answer is always yes, in front of every input, teaches the user to approve without reading, and the gate is then worth nothing on the writes it exists for").

findings.description: Both greps hit, the invocation is shown in the `<skill-path>` convention in its own section between phase 4 and phase 5, and all three requirements hold — including the phase-4 boundary, which is stated as a convention and explicitly conceded to be non-forced.
findings.evidence: Greps: `/usr/bin/grep -n 'scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh' inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md` -> `145:bash <skill-path>/scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh <scope-root> \`; `/usr/bin/grep -n 'require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh"' tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` -> `301:require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh"`. Placement: heading scan puts `### Phase 4` at :132, `### Stamp Confirmations` at :140, `### Phase 5` at :160, so the call is outside phase 2.5's "For each inbox file" loop and ahead of the gate, not buried in phase 6's verify list. (1) :152 — "**One call for the whole queue, never one per input.** Hand it every group at once. Two inputs in one run can confirm the same record, and the script only gets to write that record once — taking the later of the two dates — if it sees both groups in the same invocation." (2) :154 — "**A run that found no confirmations makes no call at all**, and most runs are that run. An invocation with no `--note` group is a usage error rather than a quiet no-op, so there is nothing to hand it and nothing to run." (3) :156 — "Putting the call here, after phase 4 and before phase 5, is a convention rather than something the script forces. The close of phase 3 would serve as well, since phase 4 only disposes sources and opens no gate. ... the batch rule above is the part that carries real weight." No claim anywhere that the boundary is forced; the concession matches C-17's own text.

findings.description: The consumer suite exits 0, and it did so without any existing assertion being softened: exactly one assertion was added and none reworded.
findings.evidence: `bash tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh; echo "suite exit=$?"` -> `inbox-to-memory smoke: ok` / `suite exit=0`. Assertion census: `grep -c 'require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md'` returns 28 in the working tree against 27 at `git show 924f81f:tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` — a net +1. `git diff --numstat tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` is `2 1`, and the word-diff shows the only edits are a comment reword (`lint,`->`scripts it runs,`, `it`->`them`) plus the new line `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh"`. No pinned string was moved or weakened: all five survive verbatim at exactly one occurrence each (`grep -Fc` returns 1 for "one sanctioned exception to preserving raw content", "**Five body reads per input, and the budget binds.**", "### Phase 2.5 — Check Against Accepted Memory", "**Normalize them through the scope's alias table** before any lookup", and "read budget bound is named"). The new assertion is not vacuous: `git show 924f81f:inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md | grep -Fq 'scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh'` exits 1, so it would have reddened the suite against the base tree, and `require_text` at :28-35 exits 1 on a miss.
